liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Feel Like a Stranger** (2 reviews): Reviewer was blown away by the opening Stranger; First set opened with Stranger and started decently, but got weaker afterward [27][30]
- **Just Like Tom Thumb's Blues** (2 reviews): Reviewer rates the Tom Thumb's Blues as great; Reviewer is thrilled that Tom Thumb's Blues follows the space after Going Down the Road [26][37]
- **Scarlet Begonias** (1 review): From the first notes of Scarlet, reviewer was up dancing like never before [36]
- **Looks Like Rain** (1 review): Looks Like Rain was pretty good, helped by booming bass [32]
- **Black Peter** (1 review): Reviewer says Black Peter alone was worth the ticket price [37]

## The recordings

- **gd86-03-25.sbd.braverman-munder.9880.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 19 songs; 134 min; rated 3.5/5 by 8 [1]. Said about its sound: The soundboard sounds good, though the band stumbled through the show; Reviewer calls the soundboard sound absolutely grand [28][37]
- **gd1986-03-25.sbd.braverman.9404.shnf**: soundboard; 19 songs; 134 min [2]
- **gd1986-03-25.176167.sbd.donaldson.miller.clugston.flac1648**: soundboard; 19 songs; 137 min [3]
- **gd1986-03-25.151098.senn441.mattes.miller.clugston.flac1648**: audience recording; 19 songs; 137 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [5]
- **gd86-03-25.beyer.connor.3188.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 19 songs; 127 min; rated 3.73/5 by 10 [10]. Said about its sound: Sound quality on this audience recording is good; The space before Scarlet sounds cut on this copy [33]

## Around the show

- Reviewer says this was the last general-admission Dead show at the Spectrum, and their first show [27]
- Second set opened with entertaining space jamming [30]
- Reviewer stood near Jerry; the tuneup/noise jam into set two ran long, with a whispered 'hurry' [32]
- Reviewer first saw the Dead in 1981; this 1986 show was when it finally clicked for them [34]
- Reviewer first saw the Dead in 1981; this 1986 show was when it finally clicked for them [35]
- Reviewer arrived late with their brother, hearing the end of set one from behind the stage [36]
- Disc two runs over 80 minutes, so the encore can move to disc one [1]
- Reviewer likes that the setlist departs from what had become routine by 1986 [26]
- The previous night's soundboard sounds poor even though the band played well that night [28]
- Reviewer ranks it the worst of 37 shows attended from 1981 to 1995, possibly the worst of the 1980s [30]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd86-03-25.sbd.braverman-munder.9880.sbeok.shnf**: source: Shntool fix by Willy of previous Braverman seed [1]. Also: Soundboard to master cassette to DAT to CD to SHN, with a Shntool fix by Willy [1]
- **gd1986-03-25.sbd.braverman.9404.shnf**: transferred by Rob Harrison and Peter Braverman; source: Soundboard [2]. Also: Desolation Row begins abruptly at the vocal because of a tape flip; Discs came from Rob Harrison; Peter Braverman seeded this version in May 2002 [2]
- **gd1986-03-25.176167.sbd.donaldson.miller.clugston.flac1648**: taped by Dougal Donaldson; transferred by Scott Clugston, Charlie Miller; source: Soundboard > VHS Master (Sony Handycam)(Stereo) > Dougal Donaldson's 1st Generation Cassettes > Sony TC-D5M (Maxell XLIIS-90 (Dolby B) [3]. Also: Charlie Connor's Beyer M88 recording patches gaps in the Roses/Desolation Row transition and in space [3]
- **gd1986-03-25.151098.senn441.mattes.miller.clugston.flac1648**: taped by Ted Mattes; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: Ted Mattes' Master Audience Cassettes; Sennheiser 441 mics > Sony D5M [5]. Also: Charlie Connor's Beyer M88 source supplies the beginning of Desolation Row [5]
- **gd86-03-25.beyer.connor.3188.sbeok.shnf**: source: AUD FOB (30ft Center Stage)> Beyer Dynamic M88's> Sony TCD5M(CM)> Nak DR-10 (Playback)> Midiman Flying Cow 24bit/48kHz A/D> RME Digi96/8> Steinberg's Wavelab… [10]

Reviewer ranks it the worst of 37 shows attended from 1981 to 1995, possibly the worst of the 1980s
